evidence.detail:
For series-now, only distinct candidate subjects with a fork event in the supplied input
count toward an actor's or the authority's `open` and `owed`; a parsed name alone is insufficient.
For series-runs, a candidate also needs a fork event and a matching claim burst to belong to a
run. Forkless pushes and verdicts do not add candidates, verdict counts, timing samples, or
extend a run's `ended`. Claim and slot counts still come from the claims themselves.

why_now.summary: Every check passed. The amendment changes the spec text that every later run reads.

evidence.summary: The amendment adds 6 lines and removes none. It cites ADMIT on series-now at 2026-10-09T03:19:08.913Z. The replay result: cites a recorded ADMIT; nothing to replay.
evidence.detail:
In series-now, a verdict always updates the authority's latest activity. It updates the
candidate owner's latest activity only when that candidate has a fork event somewhere in the
supplied input. Without that fork, a verdict neither creates an owner row nor updates an
existing owner row. A candidate main or submitter-notes push can still create or update its
owner's activity without a fork, but contributes no candidate to `open` or `owed`.

evidence.summary: The amendment adds 6 lines and removes none. It cites ADMIT on series-runs at 2026-10-09T03:15:31.259Z. The replay result: cites a recorded ADMIT; nothing to replay.
evidence.detail:
For series-now and series-runs, the latest verdict of one candidate is the verdict with
the greatest `at`. If that candidate has multiple verdicts at the same greatest time, the
last one in the supplied event list wins. There is no verdict-name precedence for this tie.
This determines latest-verdict counts and states; it does not change series-feed's ordering
between event kinds or subjects.

why_now.summary: Every check passed. The amendment changes the spec text that every later run reads.

evidence.summary: The amendment adds 7 lines and removes none. It cites ADMIT on series-runs at 2026-10-09T03:15:31.259Z. The replay result: cites a recorded ADMIT; nothing to replay.
evidence.detail:
The run median includes only candidates whose latest verdict is ADMIT and which have
both a main-branch push and an ADMIT timestamp. Each included sample is seconds from that
candidate's earliest main push to its earliest ADMIT, rounded to the nearest integer.
A historical ADMIT followed by a later REFUSE or SEND_BACK contributes no sample. Samples
sort numerically and use nearest-rank p50: for an even count, the lower middle value; with
no eligible samples the median is null.

A historical ADMIT followed by a later REFUSE or SEND_BACK contributes no sample. Samples
sort numerically and use nearest-rank p50: for an even count, the lower middle value; with

evidence.detail:
In series-feed, a push not covered by a candidate main, submitter-notes, or admission-note
case uses the canonical main, tag, or notes wording when its ref matches those cases, even
when its subject parses as a candidate. Otherwise its LINE is `<repo> <full-ref>: <message>`.
An absent, null, or empty ref uses `push` in place of `<full-ref>`; an absent or null message
omits the colon and message. These other-ref pushes have ACTOR `authority` and remain feed
items; they are not discarded for lacking a table row.

evidence.summary: The amendment adds 7 lines and removes none. It cites ADMIT on view-runs at 2026-10-09T03:13:42.846Z. The replay result: cites a recorded ADMIT; nothing to replay.
evidence.detail:
The admitted now, feed, and runs modules put their finding first and render in normal
document flow. The now view renders all actor rows; the runs view renders all run cards in
a grid that wraps to the available width. These modules enforce no fixed viewport height
or clipping limit, so a growing payload can require scrolling. The feed initially displays
25 events and places any remaining supplied events in a closed native `details` disclosure.
There is no additional disclosure or truncation rule for the now or runs payloads.

evidence.summary: The amendment adds 8 lines and removes none. It cites ADMIT on series-now at 2026-10-09T03:19:08.913Z. The replay result: cites a recorded ADMIT; nothing to replay.
evidence.detail:
A ruling describes the checks at its `ruled_at`; it is not an immutable verdict about
every future authority version. An authority repair to its reference or input generator can
be followed by an ADMIT of an existing candidate tip, without a candidate-code change.
The recorded series-now ADMIT of `adff4bdeccf07f14ebfb3357d274ceb3fca6e566` is such a tip.
Earlier rulings remain historical records, but do not by themselves establish a current
reproducible failure. Amendments citing a SEND_BACK must meet the current replay check;
an ADMIT citation is the recorded measurement and is not replayed.
